subject: MAP: POC environment close plan — org seeds, ephemeral keys, allowlist & peering
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <claire@lumence.com>, Raj Patel <raj@lumence.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: POC environment close plan — org seeds, ephemeral keys, allowlist & peering

Claire / Raj,

Great to recap our call this morning. Per our mutual action plan I put together a concise checklist so we can close the POC and validate latency/cost across your production-like workloads. High level asks from Lumence and owners on our side below. I attached a one-page MAP and the network allowlist template.

Summary / owner calls-to-action:
- Org seed + service accounts (Lumence): create org admin and two dev service accounts. Send the org ID to us (owner: Claire).
- API keys (Redwood): we will create ephemeral API keys scoped to the POC workspace and rotate every 24h. Ben to share initial keys and rotate cadence.
- IP allowlist (Lumence): populate network-allowlist-template.csv (attachment) with NAT egress IPs for your test subnet.
- VPC peering (Optional, parallel path): if you want private peering for throughput tests, share your VPC CIDR and target region; Neha will propose peering window.
- Acceptance test (Joint): run 3 representative evals (chat, long generation, embedding) — pass thresholds: median p95 latency < 320ms and cost per 1k tokens within target.

Proposed close timeline (target):
- 8/24: Lumence returns org ID + filled allowlist template
- 8/26: Redwood provides initial ephemeral keys + peering proposal
- 8/28: Joint canary run + pass/fail report

Please reply with any blockers. If the peering path is sensitive, we can defer and run over public endpoints with prefix/KV caching.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: 415-555-0142
redwood.ai

Attachments: MAP-Lumence-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-allowlist-template.csv (csv), redwood-soc2-evidence-summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Claire Zhang <claire@lumence.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@lumence.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2029 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment close plan — org seeds, ephemeral keys, allowlist & peering

Tessa — thanks, this looks good and very actionable. Quick clarifications: 

1) For org ID, do you need a specific format (project vs organization)? We'll send the Lumence tenant id and a service-account email.
2) On ephemeral keys — will Redwood provide a short-lived token for our CI jobs, or do you expect us to fetch tokens dynamically from your endpoint? We prefer not to bake long-lived keys into CI.
3) VPC peering: Raj flagged that we need to route peering through our staging VPC (10.32.0.0/16). Is that acceptable?

We'll aim to fill the allowlist template and send it by EOD 8/24. If you can confirm the answers above, we can lock the timeline.

Best,
Claire
Sr. Platform Engineer, Lumence Health
claire@lumence.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <claire@lumence.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Raj Patel <raj@lumence.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2029 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment close plan — org seeds, ephemeral keys, allowlist & peering

Claire — quick answers inline: 

1) Org ID: the tenant ID (org level) and one service-account email is perfect; we'll use that to bind permissions for the POC workspace.

2) Ephemeral keys: Redwood will provide short-lived tokens (12–24 hours) and a small helper script (shell + curl) that your CI can call to exchange for a token. We will not require long-lived keys. We can also support an on-prem fetch approach if you want a managed exchange via your key manager.

3) VPC peering: 10.32.0.0/16 is fine — Neha, please propose a peering window and any IPs we should add to our side.

I'll prepare the first set of ephemeral keys once we have the org ID — expect an encrypted share via our secure link.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <claire@lumence.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Aug 2029 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment close plan — org seeds, ephemeral keys, allowlist & peering

Claire / Raj — dropping a short peering ops checklist and preferred windows. If peering is greenlit we'll run a brief connectivity test, then a throughput/latency test during the canary.

Peering checklist (Redwood side):
- Confirm Lumence VPC CIDR: 10.32.0.0/16 (confirmed by Claire)
- Provide Lumence peering contact + ticketing window (preferred: 8/26 14:00–16:00 PT)
- Add Redwood staging egress IPs to allowlist (see template) — we will provide the final egress IP list on 8/26 morning.
- Cross-check routing rules & security groups; we do not open management ports — only peering routes and test ports.

If you prefer to avoid peering for now we can proceed on public endpoints with pre-warmed caches; you'll still see realistic latency numbers but not the private-network tail.

I'll schedule a 30-min ops slot for 8/26 14:00 PT for the peering handshake. RSVP please.

Neha Kapoor
Infra Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Raj Patel <raj@lumence.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Claire Zhang <claire@lumence.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Aug 2029 15:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment close plan — org seeds, ephemeral keys, allowlist & peering

Team — quick wrap. We completed the allowlist and shared the CSV on 8/24. Peering window on 8/26 worked; we saw stable p95 numbers but need one follow-up: embedding throughput spikes under batched requests. Can Ben/Neha propose a tuning pass (batch size / kv cache policy) and an updated cost run for 10k request samples?

If Redwood can provide the tuning suggestions and a short runbook, we can sign the POC acceptance on our side. Also: please upload the SOC-2 summary to the shared Drive link for our internal audit.

Thanks — Raj
Head of Platform, Lumence Health
raj@lumence.com
